surprises.description: The preview expected FTE NIM of about 4.42–4.45%, but CBC reported 4.51%; net interest income was also $218.9 million versus the preview’s roughly $217 million estimate. The margin came in above the preview’s range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest income rose $20 million year-over-year to $218.9 million, with FTE net interest margin expanding 12 basis points to 4.51%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “My estimate: … NII ~$217M (FTE NIM 4.42–4.45%).” The preview also flagged “FTE NIM vs. ~4.45% whisper.”

surprises.description: The preview’s consensus was $0.49 per share, while CBC reported $0.48. That was a small miss, although it was within the preview’s own $0.48–$0.49 estimate range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 net income was $116.2 million, or $0.48 per share.”

surprises.description: The preview looked for at least 5–6% annualized loan growth excluding consumer loans, and its base case assumed 4–6%. CBC reported 3% linked-quarter annualized growth overall and about 4% excluding declining indirect consumer loans, slightly below that range.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loans grew 3% linked-quarter annualized (about 4% excluding declining indirect consumer loans).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Need ≥5–6% annualized ex-consumer plus commercial pipeline confirmation.” The base case also assumed “loans +4–6% ann. ex-consumer.”

surprises.description: The preview cited net charge-offs of 10 basis points and expected them to remain steady. CBC reported 12 basis points, a slight deterioration, though management said credit remained benign and saw no thematic shift in risk.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net charge-offs remained benign at just 12 basis points for the quarter, and management sees no thematic shift in credit risk.”

surprises.description: The preview estimated an efficiency ratio of about 46%, while CBC reported 45.4%, indicating somewhat better efficiency than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The FTE efficiency ratio [was] at a strong 45.4%.”

surprises.description: The preview did not anticipate a pension-related gain. CBC said it expects a nonrecurring pretax gain of approximately $27 million in Q4 after contracting the plan termination payments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company expects to record a nonrecurring pretax gain of approximately $27 million in Q4 from terminating its frozen pension plan, with termination payments now contracted.”

surprises.description: The preview was concerned that deposit costs might not stay anchored through a rising-rate cycle. CBC reported deposit costs down 8 basis points year-over-year and management expected a mid- to low-20s deposit beta if rates rise, offering a more favorable deposit-cost outlook than that concern implied.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Cost of deposits fell 8 basis points year-over-year, and management expects a mid- to low-20s deposit beta in a rising-rate environment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Watch whether deposit cost (1.10%, 36% noninterest-bearing) stays anchored.”

surprises.description: The preview emphasized intermediate-curve pressure on spreads and cited $1.3 billion of loans repricing in H2 2026. CBC also described a cash flow hedge placed at quarter-end, but disclosed a future repricing tailwind: $2.2 billion of loans in 2027 rolling off rates near 6% into yields roughly 100 basis points higher. The hedge and higher-yield resets create a more balanced outlook than the preview’s rate-compression concern alone suggested.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The bank remains slightly asset-sensitive and placed a cash flow hedge at quarter-end, with $700 million of fixed loans repricing in Q4 and $2.2 billion in 2027 rolling off a ~6% rate into yields roughly 100 bps higher.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “CFO Ciroli explicitly flagged intermediate-curve sensitivity — sharp rate increases compress spreads.” The preview also cited “$1.3B of loans reprice in H2'26 at a 5.8% yield.”
